reason: The load-bearing mechanism (dotted-username truncation) is false for the installed driver. postgres@3.4.9 parseUrl (node_modules/.pnpm/postgres@3.4.9/node_modules/postgres/src/index.js:537-556) does exactly what db/index.ts parseDbUrl does: const urlObj = new URL(url); username: decodeURIComponent(urlObj.username). Ran postgres("postgresql://postgres.abcdefgh:pw%40ss@aws-0-us-west-1.pooler.supabase.com:5432/postgres").options and got user="postgres.abcdefgh" (full, untruncated), pass="pw@ss", host=aws-0-us-west-1.pooler.supabase.com, port=5432, db=postgres. So migrate.ts authenticates with the SAME credentials as the app; migrations do not fail on the pooler URL. The db/index.ts:9-11 comment the reviewer relied on is stale (reviewer admitted it was not re-tested). Residual real-but-minor divergence: postgres.js defaults ssl:false, so migrate.ts gets no TLS on a supabase host unless the URL carries ?sslmode=require (verified: sslmode=require in the URL yields ssl="require"), whereas db/index.ts forces ssl:"require". That is a TLS-posture inconsistency worth fixing, not a deploy-gate auth failure.
